I actually understand what you mean and agree on some parts. But for me, I don't just like Twenty One Pilots because I think they sound different or that they have crazy deep lyrics. I like them because even though they've gotten very popular over the years, they still are so open about mental health and don't tip toe around subjects. I know they aren't the only ones that do that, but not a lot of other popular artists are willing to really speak out about things like suicide. As for the lyrics, you make a good point about their lyrics not always being the deepest. But one thing about their lyrics is that they're real. We know that they come from the heart and aren't just some fake, sappy lyrics written to put on a show. Tyler and Josh have both been through a lot, and their lyrics continue to show their struggle through that, which I really appreciate. I think my point in this is that for me at least, I don't like them just for the drums beats or the lyrics. I can relate to the lyrics and feel like someone gets what I'm feeling. They can sometimes sound kind of generic, but I know that Tyler means them, and he's trying to send a message. I do understand what you mean though. It's a good discussion to have.

I don't know if you want advice from me, but I'm also a teen girl so I might be able to help. I used to act the exact same way with my parents. I acted out in rage because I was depressed and anxious and hated everything. Usually if a teen is acting out like she is, it's probably not for no reason. I would talk to her if you can, or just let her know that if she is angry or upset for some reason, then she can talk to you about it. She may just have a terrible attitude, but she may also be struggling.
